thread:
maya: Quick design question for envelope encryption on Private deployments — trying to lock down DEK/KEK boundaries and reduce KMS traffic. Thoughts?
liam: short answer: DEK per-object, KEK in KMS. but we need to define cache TTL and refresh triggers.
sarah: agree on per-object DEKs. also consider a small-tiered cache: in-memory hot cache + local encrypted LRU backed by disk for rest.
maya: yea. two things I'm worried about: 1) KMS call frequency during bulk ingestion, 2) audit trails for key operations (who/why). any policies we should follow?
anish: for audit: require write-through logs to central auditing for every KEK unwrap/rotate, but we don't need an audit entry for every DEK usage if it's local-only. instead log DEK creation + occasional attestations.
liam: for KMS calls: batch unwraps where possible. pattern: store DEKs wrapped by KEK; on read, if DEK in cache serve; if cache-miss, fetch wrapped DEKs from blobstore and call KMS to unwrap. avoid calling KMS per token.
sarah: implement exponential backoff + jitter in unwrap retry to avoid thundering herd during cold-starts. also add circuit-breaker to fail-safe to a slower path (e.g., synchronous admin approval) if KMS is unreachable.
maya: what about TTL on cached plaintext DEKs? how long is acceptable before we re-unwrap to ensure forward secrecy and limit plaintext exposure?
liam: propose default TTL = 15m for in-memory plaintext DEKs, configurable per-customer. Add a max TTL of 6h for private customers with compliance opt-in. On rotation event or KEK revocation, purge immediately.
sarah: plus a sliding window refresh: if a DEK was last used < 80% of TTL, don't proactively refresh. If usage spikes, we can keep it warm without re-unwrapping each time.
maya: ok. encryption-at-rest on the cache itself? we should encrypt in-memory backup or disk LRU with OS-protected key and tie to host TPM if available.
liam: yes: disk LRU encrypted with a host key (HSM/TMP/KMS-derived). In-memory plaintext only lives in process heap; on eviction zero-out buffer. Use secure_alloc APIs.
anish: RBAC change: we'll need a new role `kms-unwrapper` scoped to service identities that are allowed to unwrap KEKs. Also require MFA for any human principals that can trigger rotations.
audit-bot: Audit log: new entries created for `KEK_UNWRAP`, `KEK_ROTATE`, `DEK_GENERATE` with fields: principal, key_id, request_id, src_ip.
maya: good — are we ok with logging request metadata but avoid logging the plaintext DEK material (obviously)?
sarah: definitely never log raw DEKs. Log only hashes (SHA256) of DEK for correlation if needed.
liam: KMS rate-limits: add local rate limiter per-instance + token-bucket shared across pods in a region. fallback to queued unwraps with prioritization for recent traffic.
maya: edge-case: if a KEK rotates mid-traffic, how do we handle concurrent operations on objects wrapped with old KEK?
liam: plan: rotate KEK by creating new KEK, update wrap policies for new DEKs. Old DEKs remain readable by adding a key policy that allows decrypt with old KEK for a migration window (e.g., 30 days) then rewrap DEKs lazily during access.
sarah: lazy rewrap on access is easiest; run background rewrap job for cold items. ensure rewrap job uses dedicated credentials and respects rate limits.
anish: incident response note: if KMS suspected compromise, we must revoke KEK usage and fail-safe to sealed-mode: deny direct unwraps and require offline recovery. document playbook.
maya: can we add telemetry for unwrap latencies so SRE can alert on KMS degradation before errors spike?
liam: yes, emit metrics: unwrap_time_ms, unwrap_error_rate, cache_hit_rate. alert on unwrap_error_rate > 1% for 5m or cache_hit_rate < 60%.
sarah: one more: for GCP/Azure compatibility, wrap/unwrap APIs differ. create an adapter layer that normalizes audit fields and errors so our logic stays unified.
maya: actionable items: liam to draft cache TTL defaults + eviction/encryption details; sarah to write unwrap retry/circuit-breaker pseudocode; anish to propose RBAC role + audit fields. I'll collate and drive doc PR.
liam: will do, I'll post a config snippet.
liam: ```yaml
# unpack-cache example
plaintext_dek_ttl: 900 # seconds
max_plaintext_dek_ttl: 21600 # seconds
cache_size_entries: 10000
disk_backed: true
disk_encrypt: true
unwrap_rate_limit_per_instance: 20 # rps
shared_bucket_capacity: 200
``` 
maya: awesome. tagging @sarah @anish for follow-ups. thanks folks :rocket:
audit-bot: created issue SEC-ENCRYPT-872 for follow-up doc and playbook.
